correctness.rationale: Permutation averaging preserves the range and fixes every circulation, and by convexity cannot increase either norm. The four stabilizer orbits of an edge leave only one scalar after the row and column constraints, and fixing a nonzero four-cycle fixes that scalar, so the average is Q. The all-p tensor norm follows by acting on separate fibers and testing on a rank-one matrix made of norming vectors, including p=1 and infinity. Writing α=(m−1)(n−1)/(mn), the diagonal and each of the three off-diagonal absolute blocks of a column contribute α to Q; the complement contributes 1−α on the diagonal and 3α off it. Symmetry gives the row sums, and the tie is exactly (m−2)(n−2)=2 at the two endpoint exponents. At p=2 both projections are nonzero orthogonal projections. The source script was inspected, not executed; finite tests are not needed for these universal arguments.
